sets.name: Western zodiac
sets.review: One grain and one shape across the twelve (29-32 words; a gloss of the sign's drive, a colon, four or five behaviors from the keyword list in roughly its flattering/unflattering proportion); no member at a different grain. Ring: agree that the calendar order is not a similarity order and that what is readable is the element cycle: earth (Taurus solid, Virgo exacting, Capricorn grounded) and water (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces all open on feeling or intensity) read plainly, fire (charging, royalty, on the go) by energy and warmth, air least (Gemini's talk, Libra's balance, Aquarius's ideas share only mind and sociability); good enough, and nothing names an element. Sources: every passage is Cafe Astrology's keyword list plus the opening of its 'Sun in' section, with astrology.com as the cross-check, since Wikipedia carries no portraits; agreed, that was the packet's fallback. But eight drafts take a clause from the cross-check rather than the passage: Scorpio three clauses, its whole fault side ('keeping one's own hidden', 'slow to trust', 'not forgetting a wrong'); Leo 'loving the limelight' and 'proud'; Pisces 'easily wounded'; Cancer 'home'; Aries 'quick to anger' (short temper; not flagged in its notes); Libra 'balance', 'weighing every side'; Taurus 'comfort'; Virgo's opening 'exacting', which the passage itself says is rare in modern Virgos. Each is the conventional attribute and each is quoted in notes, so I accept the text; the record is the problem: source_text should carry the quoted astrology.com phrase wherever a draft rests on it (Scorpio above all), and the file's `source` should name both sites, or a later reader will find the file citing Cafe Astrology for content it does not contain. The writer's flags: agree that Capricorn, Leo and Pisces are faithful to passages with no fault side (Capricorn's only non-compliment is 'conservative', Leo's text half-denies the conceit, Pisces's soft fault is 'impressionable') and so come out more flattering than the cross-check; agree that Scorpio is the least flattering of the twelve. But the asymmetry is the writer's own: Scorpio's faults were lifted from the cross-check and the other three signs' were not (Capricorn: stubbornness, judgment, miserliness; Leo: vanity, jealousy; Pisces: escapism, codependence), so the set's fault side is uneven in a way the sources are not. Options for Roger: (a) keep the drafts as they stand with the record completed; (b) lift one conventional fault into each of the three, inside 32 words: Capricorn 'disciplined, prudent and stubbornly tenacious' (cross-check: 'dedicated to their goals, almost to the point of stubbornness'); Leo '... loving the limelight, vain, and proud enough to be taken for conceited'; Pisces '... open-minded and understanding, easily wounded, and quick to escape into fantasy'; (c) trim Scorpio to its passage. I lean to (b), since the method's target for a folk system is the conventional portrait and the three signs' conventional portraits do carry those faults; (a) is defensible; (c) is not, because the conventional Scorpio does carry suspicion and a long memory. Per-entry edits: Aquarius (one hedge flattened) and Sagittarius ('irresponsible', its one hard fault, dropped); Scorpio marked edit for the record, not the text.

sets.name: Enneagram
sets.review: One grain and one shape (29-32 words; the type's drive, a colon, the Institute's adjectives and faults in the source's order); nicknames and the system unnamed throughout; no member at a different grain. Ring: the figure's numbering is the order and the drafts keep it readable; agree that the three triads show without being named (8-9-1 anger as hot temper, stubbornness, resentment; 2-3-4 being needed, admired, distinct; 5-6-7 head types in isolation, anxiety and chasing experience), and neighbors read as wings where the system has them (3-4 image and identity, 4-5 withdrawal, 5-6 thinking and fear). 'At their Best' omitted across all nine: agree. It is the type at its healthiest, an aspiration rather than the portrait, and its sentences are generic (heroic, inspiring, visionary) so including them would tilt every type flattering and blur the nine; uniform omission keeps the set balanced, and the sentence stays in source_text for the record. The file's `source` should say the 'in Brief' paragraph was summarised and 'At their Best' left out, so a later reader does not take the omission for an oversight. Disagree with the set_review's claim that the source's hedges were rendered rather than dropped. 'Sometimes' (type 8, 'at times') and 'too willing' (type 9, 'too readily') were rendered; the paragraphs' structural hedge on every fault clause, 'but can also be', 'can slip into', 'can become', is dropped in types 2 through 9 and kept only in type 1 ('slipping into'), and type 2's notes say the flattening was deliberate. Where the flattened fault is also in the Institute's unhedged one-liner (Perfectionistic, Possessive, Image-Conscious, Temperamental, Isolated, Suspicious, Scattered, Confrontational, Complacent) the flat form has flat support and I let it stand, which clears types 1, 3, 5, 6 and 9 on this point; where it has none (2: helping to be needed, flattering; 4: disdainful and exempt; 7: over-extended, undisciplined, exhausted; 8: 'unable' for 'problems with') I ask for the hedge back in two words or fewer, edits supplied at 31-32 words. Roger may rule instead that the one-liner licenses flat faults throughout; the edits for 7 ('never stopping') and 8 ('unable') are sharpenings of wording that stand regardless. Balance: the drafts keep about four of each passage's six or seven virtues and about five of its five or six faults (the virtue side was trimmed for length, the fault side kept nearly whole), so the set sits a notch harsher than the Institute's paragraphs; the writer is right that this is about the corpus's plain-trait strength, but it is not quite 'at source'. The Nine is the extreme (two virtues, all five faults; edit supplied adds 'supportive'), the Two next (edit adds 'generous'). Items dropped for length are named in each entry's notes, as the packet asked; I checked them and none leaves a type unrecognisable.

sets.name: Holland RIASEC
sets.review: Clean. One grain and one shape (28-32 words; 'This means being drawn to work that ...', a gloss of the kind of work, then O*NET's activities and fields); all six from the same descriptor pages, so no member has a different grain of source; neutral strength uniformly, as the instrument is, and uniformly milder than the corpus's plain traits, which is the instrument's nature. The ring in RIASEC order is readable off the drafts (hands and machines, study and research, making something original, work done for other people, deals and leading, data in order by procedure, and back to hands), and Prediger's two axes read off it without being seeded: Things against People is realistic against social, Data against Ideas is conventional and enterprising (office, business) against investigative and artistic (research, original work), which settles the queue's Prediger note as intended. Nearest existing: artistic and conventional are deliberate by-name near-duplicates and the lines say so; each file's `source` must record that (rule 5). One nuance: the plain `conventional` (read) is about reaching for the standard answer and the template and distrusting anything original, not 'conforming to social norms' as the writer's line puts it; the distinction from the Holland sense (a vocational interest in procedural, data-ordering office work) holds either way. The plain `artistic` (read) is a maker's temperament ('judging a day by what got made'); the Holland version is a vocational pull; the distinction holds. Two small wordings, not worth an edit on their own: social's 'religious life' in common use means the life of monks and nuns, where O*NET's 'religious activities' is broader ('religious work' is exact); investigative's 'work of study and research: into ...' reads a little stiffly across the colon. Take them if the files are touched for another reason. The Interest Profiler's person-oriented wording was not fetchable, so the inside voice is the writer's uniform bridge 'being drawn to work that', which is acceptable and consistent.

summary:
27 drafts, all inside the form (28-32 words, one sentence, 'This means', nothing named, US spelling); every nearest-existing stem exists and the two by-name near-duplicates (artistic, conventional) are declared. 19 ok, 8 edit.
Edits: Aquarius (one hedge flattened); Sagittarius ('irresponsible', its one hard fault, dropped); Enneagram 2, 4, 7, 8 (the Institute's 'can also be' flattened where the one-liner gives no flat support; 'never stopping' and 'unable' sharpened); Enneagram 9 (virtues cut to two, all five faults kept); Scorpio for the record, not the text (its whole fault side is the astrology.com cross-check and must go into source_text).
Sets: Holland clean, ring and Prediger axes readable. Zodiac one grain, elements readable; the writer's flags hold (Capricorn, Leo, Pisces faithful to fault-free passages; Scorpio harshest) but the asymmetry is the writer's own, Scorpio's faults lifted from the cross-check and the other three's not, so Roger chooses between leaving it and lifting one conventional fault each (wordings in the set review).
Enneagram one grain, ring and triads readable, the 'At their Best' omission right (record it in `source`); I disagree that hedges were rendered rather than dropped, and the set sits a notch harsher than its paragraphs. For the parent: wherever a zodiac draft rests on astrology.com, append the quoted phrase to source_text and name both sites in `source`.
